author: claude
hook_line: A koala's fingerprints could fool a crime lab, and that is not even the weird part.
intro: A koala's fingerprints could fool a crime lab, and that is not even the weird part.
facts: Koalas have fingerprints with loops and whorls so similar to ours that even under a microscope experts struggle to tell a koala print from a human one.
They sleep up to 20 hours a day, not because they are lazy, but because eucalyptus leaves are toxic and so low in energy that digesting them takes almost everything they have.
A koala is not a bear at all but a marsupial, and a newborn joey is about the size of a jelly bean, crawling blind into its mother's pouch to keep growing.
Before a joey can eat leaves it eats a special soft dropping from its mother, called pap, which loads its gut with the bacteria needed to survive on eucalyptus.
outro: Not a bear, and definitely not lazy.
